concept: Riverside cafe street under a striped sky of memory and reflection
scene: An off-white risograph poster shows a nocturnal riverside street that turns into an open-air cafe and record-transfer workshop in one continuous setting, with a strong diagonal running from lower left to upper right. In the lower left, a simplified scooter with a cluster of round mirrors is parked at the curb, its mirrors catching tiny flat face silhouettes and its exhaust becoming grainy clouds that drift upward across the whole image. Those clouds merge into a striped evening sky made of broad horizontal bands borrowed from the warm striped portrait, overprinted so the orange and yellow become a glowing dusk behind deep blue. Along the diagonal cobblestone path, three coat-clad adult walkers move uphill past cafe windows and sparse reeds, their steps echoing the street scene while one elongated standing figure in a sweater vest leans near the edge of the pavement like a watchful passerby. At mid-right, the diner and street blend together: a counter window opens onto the cobbles, where a pompadoured tattooed man and a dark-haired woman appear as separate seated silhouettes inside, framed by condiment shapes and booth backs rather than posed portraits. Above them, pinned to a cafe awning and partly dissolving into the smoke, a doubled downward-looking curly-haired face becomes a pasted billboard image, printed as two near-identical panels. In the upper right, a large translucent production sheet hangs like a shop sign or drafting screen over the street, carrying a blue line-drawn suited figure, registration crosses, arrows, and technical boxes, as if the whole neighborhood is being mapped in real time. Reeds cut into the sky at the far edges, tying the street to the open air. Everything is reduced to bold flat shapes, halftone grain, and slight misregistration in sunflower yellow, burnt orange, and cobalt blue inks.
prompt: Create one bold risograph print - flat layered shapes, coarse riso grain, overlapping translucent inks slightly out of register, paper texture showing through. The image is a 16:9 music blog header.
